-- FORMAT-START-9F3A
{-# LANGUAGE TupleSections #-}

minimizeTestcases :: Int -> Int -> [Int] -> [Int] -> (Int, [[Int]])
-- FORMAT-SIGNATURE-9F3A
minimizeTestcases n k mList cList = (length testcases, testcases)
  where
    -- Pair each array size with its index for tracking
    indexedArrays = zip [0..] mList
    -- Initialize the list of testcases as empty
    initialTestcases = []

    -- Function to check if a candidate number of testcases is feasible
    feasible :: Int -> [[Int]] -> Bool
    feasible m testcases = all (\i -> countGe i testcases <= cList !! (i - 1)) [1..k]
      where
        countGe i tcs = sum [length (filter (\size -> size >= i) tc) | tc <- tcs]

    -- Binary search for minimal number of testcases
    binarySearch :: Int -> Int -> [[Int]] -> [[Int]]
    binarySearch low high currentTestcases
      | low >= high = currentTestcases
      | otherwise =
          let mid = (low + high) `div` 2
              testcasesCandidate = distributeArrays mid
          in if feasible mid testcasesCandidate
             then binarySearch low mid testcasesCandidate
             else binarySearch (mid + 1) high currentTestcases

    -- Function to distribute arrays into 'm' testcases
    distributeArrays :: Int -> [[Int]]
    distributeArrays m = foldl assignArray initialBuckets sortedArrays
      where
        -- Initialize m empty testcases
        initialBuckets = replicate m []
        -- Sort arrays in descending order to assign larger arrays first
        sortedArrays = map snd $ sortBy (\(a, _) (b, _) -> compare b a) indexedArrays
        -- Assign each array to the test case with the minimal current count of arrays >= its size
        assignArray :: [[Int]] -> Int -> [[Int]]
        assignArray buckets size =
          let -- Find testcases where adding this array doesn't violate constraints
              validBuckets = filter (\b -> canAdd b size) buckets
              -- Choose the test case with minimal size
              selectedIndex = case validBuckets of
                [] -> 0
                _ -> snd $ minimumBy (\(a, _) (b, _) -> compare (length a) (length b))
                                (zip validBuckets [0..])
          in take selectedIndex buckets ++ [buckets !! selectedIndex ++ [size]] ++ drop (selectedIndex + 1) buckets

        -- Check if we can add an array of 'size' to a test case
        canAdd :: [Int] -> Int -> Bool
        canAdd tc size = all (\i -> countGE i tc <= cList !! (i - 1)) [1..size]
          where
            countGE i = length $ filter (\s -> s >= i)

    -- Perform binary search between 1 and n
    testcases = binarySearch 1 n initialTestcases
-- FORMAT-END-9F3A

-- FORMAT-START-9F3A
reconstructGenome :: [String] -> String
-- FORMAT-SIGNATURE-9F3A
import Data.List (nub, delete, find)
import Data.Maybe (fromJust, isJust)
import qualified Data.Map as Map
import qualified Data.Set as Set

reconstructGenome :: [String] -> String
reconstructGenome fragments = assembleGraph adjacencyMap startNodes
  where
    -- Extract all unique characters
    allChars = nub $ concat fragments

    -- Build adjacency map: character -> set of next characters
    adjacencyMap = buildAdjacency fragments

    -- Find nodes with no incoming edges (possible start nodes)
    startNodes = filter (\c -> not (hasIncoming c adjacencyMap)) allChars

    -- Build adjacency map from fragments
    buildAdjacency :: [String] -> Map.Map Char (Set.Set Char)
    buildAdjacency frags = foldl insertEdges Map.empty frags
      where
        insertEdges acc frag = case pairs frag of
          [] -> acc
          ps -> foldl (\m (a, b) -> Map.insertWith Set.union a (Set.singleton b) m) acc ps
        pairs s = zip s (tail s)

    -- Check if a character has incoming edges
    hasIncoming :: Char -> Map.Map Char (Set.Set Char) -> Bool
    hasIncoming c adj = any (Set.member c) (Map.elems adj)

    -- Assemble the genome starting from start nodes
    assembleGraph :: Map.Map Char (Set.Set Char) -> [Char] -> String
    assembleGraph adj starts = concatMap (dfs [] adj) starts

    -- Depth-first search to build path
    dfs :: [Char] -> Map.Map Char (Set.Set Char) -> Char -> String
    dfs visited adj current
      | current `elem` visited = ""
      | otherwise = current : case Map.lookup current adj of
          Nothing -> ""
          Just neighbors -> case find (`notElem` visited) (Set.toList neighbors) of
            Nothing -> ""
            Just nextChar -> dfs (current:visited) adj nextChar

-- FORMAT-END-9F3A

-- FORMAT-START-9F3A
data Operation = Create Int | Read Int | Update Int Int | Delete Int

-- | Performs a sequence of list operations with a maximum length constraint.
intListOperations :: Int -> [Operation] -> IO [Maybe Int]
intListOperations maxLen ops
  | maxLen < 0 = error "Maximum length cannot be negative."
  | otherwise = go [] ops
  where
    go :: [Int] -> [Operation] -> IO [Maybe Int]
    go _ [] = return []
    go lst (op:rest) = case op of
      Create val -> do
        if not (isInteger val)
          then error "Create operation requires an integer value."
          else if length lst >= maxLen
            then error "Cannot add element: list has reached maximum length."
            else go (lst ++ [val]) rest
      Read idx -> do
        if idx < 0 || idx >= length lst
          then error "Read operation: index out of range."
          else do
            let val = lst !! idx
            restResults <- go lst rest
            return (Just val : restResults)
      Update idx val -> do
        if not (isInteger val)
          then error "Update operation requires an integer value."
          else if idx < 0 || idx >= length lst
            then error "Update operation: index out of range."
            else do
              let newList = updateAt idx val lst
              go newList rest
      Delete idx -> do
        if idx < 0 || idx >= length lst
          then error "Delete operation: index out of range."
          else do
            let newList = deleteAt idx lst
            go newList rest

    isInteger :: Int -> Bool
    isInteger _ = True

    updateAt :: Int -> Int -> [Int] -> [Int]
    updateAt i v xs = take i xs ++ [v] ++ drop (i + 1) xs

    deleteAt :: Int -> [Int] -> [Int]
    deleteAt i xs = take i xs ++ drop (i + 1) xs
-- FORMAT-END-9F3A

import Data.Maybe (fromMaybe)

  { name :: String
  , frequency :: Int

  } deriving (Show, Eq)

data ParsedArgs = ParsedArgs

      { filepath = fp

      , checkComments = hasFlag ["--comments", "-c"] args
      , checkLength = hasFlag ["--length", "-l"] args
      , checkSpelling = hasFlag ["--spelling", "-s"] args
      }

    parseArgs [] = ([], [])
    parseArgs (x:xs)

matrixPower :: [[Integer]] -> Int -> [[Integer]]
matrixPower _ 0 = identityMatrix
matrixPower m n
  | n `mod` 2 == 1 = multiplyMatrices m (matrixPower m (n - 1))
  | otherwise = let half = matrixPower m (n `div` 2) in multiplyMatrices half half

-- Disjoint Set Union (Union-Find) data structure
data DSU = DSU { parent :: IM.IntMap Int, rank :: IM.IntMap Int }

emptyDSU :: Int -> DSU
emptyDSU n = DSU (IM.fromList [(i, i) | i <- [1..n]]) (IM.fromList [(i, 0) | i <- [1..n]])

find :: DSU -> Int -> (Int, DSU)
find dsu x =

minimalProduct :: Int -> [Edge] -> Int

        go dsu ((a,b,c):es) acc =

    insert x Empty = Node x Empty Empty
    insert x (Node v left right)

module FactorialModulo where

import Data.Vector.Unboxed.Mutable as M
import Data.Vector.Unboxed as V
import Control.Monad.ST

modulo :: Int
modulo = 10^9 + 7

-- Precompute factorials up to 100000 for efficiency
maxN :: Int
maxN = 100000

factorials :: V.Vector Int
factorials = runST $ do
    v <- M.new (maxN + 1)
    M.write v 0 1
    let fill i
          | i > maxN = return ()
          | otherwise = do
              prev <- M.read v (i - 1)
              M.write v i ((prev * i) `mod` modulo)
              fill (i + 1)

    V.unsafeFreeze v

factorialIterative n

    | otherwise = factorials V.! n

  where

-- FORMAT-START-9F3A
longestRegularBracketSubstring :: String -> (Int, Int)
-- FORMAT-SIGNATURE-9F3A
longestRegularBracketSubstring s = 
    let n = length s
        -- Helper function to process the string and find all valid substrings
        process :: String -> [(Int, Int)] -> [Int] -> [Int]
        process [] _ stack = []
        process (c:cs) res stack =
            case c of
                '(' -> process cs res (0:stack)
                ')' -> case stack of
                    (0:rest) -> process cs res (rest)
                    (top:rest) -> 
                        let startIdx = if top == 0 then 0 else top
                            endIdx = length res
                            newRes = take startIdx res ++ [endIdx + 1] ++ drop (startIdx + 1) res
                        in process cs newRes (0:rest)
                _ -> process cs res stack
        -- Initialize the array with zeros
        initialRes = replicate (n + 1) 0
        -- Process the string
        resArray = process s initialRes []
        -- Compute lengths of valid substrings
        lengths = [resArray !! i - resArray !! (i - 1) | i <- [1..n], resArray !! i > resArray !! (i - 1)]
        maxLen = if null lengths then 0 else maximum lengths
        count = length (filter (== maxLen) lengths)
    in if maxLen == 0 then (0, 1) else (maxLen, count)
-- FORMAT-END-9F3A

primeRange :: Int -> Int -> Bool -> [(Int, Int)]

primeRange start end includeFibonacci = 
    let
        -- Generate list of primes within the range
        primesInRange = filter isPrime [start..end]
        -- Generate Fibonacci numbers within the range
        fibsInRange = takeWhile (<= end) $ dropWhile (< start) fibonacciSequence
        fibSet = foldr (\x s -> if x >= start && x <= end then x:s else s) [] fibsInRange
        -- Filter primes based on includeFibonacci flag
        filteredPrimes = if includeFibonacci
                         then filter (`elem` fibSet) primesInRange
                         else primesInRange
        -- Pair each prime with its index
        indexedPrimes = zip filteredPrimes [0..]
    in
        indexedPrimes

-- Helper function to check for primality
isPrime :: Int -> Bool
isPrime n
    | n < 2 = False
    | otherwise = null [x | x <- [2..isqrt n], n `mod` x == 0]

-- Helper function to compute integer square root
isqrt :: Int -> Int
isqrt = floor . sqrt . fromIntegral

-- Infinite Fibonacci sequence
fibonacciSequence :: [Int]
fibonacciSequence = 0 : 1 : zipWith (+) fibonacciSequence (tail fibonacciSequence)
